journey.comment: Read the exact detected header with its bounded body keyword. journey.md#detection: The lexer then reads the header again, case-insensitively and not followed by a word character (see [The statement context](#the-statement-context)).

patterns.comment: Read a native percent comment only when its first percent is not a directive and no opening brace follows after directives. journey.md#the-statement-context: `%`, not followed by `{`: a diagram comment, from the `%` to the end of the line (see [Comments](#comments)).

Read a case-insensitive title after one whitespace character, stopping before hash, semicolon or a common-comment boundary. journey.md#the-statement-context: `title`, one whitespace character, line feed included, and one or more characters other than `#`, `;`, and a line feed: a `title` unit and a `title-text` unit, whose text is the characters after the one whitespace character.
Read an entity whole and preserve the enclosing value scope and internal directive scopes. common.md#entities: Entities do not overlap.

Read a case-insensitive section and its text up to hash, colon, semicolon or a common-comment boundary. journey.md#the-statement-context: `section`, one whitespace character, line feed included, and one or more characters other than `#`, `:`, `;`, and a line feed: a `section` unit and a `section-text` unit, whose text is the characters after the one whitespace character.
Read an entity whole and preserve the enclosing value scope and internal directive scopes. common.md#entities: Entities do not overlap.

journey-task.comment: Read task descriptions, score text, people and ignored suffixes without interpreting quoted-looking text or scores as additional token kinds. journey.md#tasks: A task is a `task-text` unit, the **description**, and its **data**: a `:` unit and the units of the data text.

Read the score as text up to the second colon or data end, including a nonnumeric score. journey.md#tasks: The **score part** runs from the first colon to the second colon or the end of the data. journey.md#tasks: A part that writes no number, such as `abc` or `5, 6`, is accepted; how mermaid.js reads the score as a number is in the summary of the tests package.
Read an entity whole and preserve the enclosing value scope and internal directive scopes. common.md#entities: Entities do not overlap.

patterns.comment: Read people as text separated by commas, leaving a third colon to begin ignored data. journey.md#tasks: The **people part** runs from the second colon, a `:` unit, to the third colon or the end of the data. journey.md#tasks: It is divided by its commas into **people**: a `,` unit for each `,`, and for each stretch between the colon, the commas, and the end of the part, a `person` unit whose text is the stretch without the whitespace at its ends, or no unit when the stretch holds only whitespace, which is an **empty person**, a null element of the task's people (see [JourneyTaskStatement](../ast/journey.md#journeytaskstatement)).
Read an entity whole and preserve the enclosing value scope and internal directive scopes. common.md#entities: Entities do not overlap.

patterns.comment: Read each people-list comma as a separator. journey.md#tasks: It is divided by its commas into **people**: a `,` unit for each `,`, and for each stretch between the colon, the commas, and the end of the part, a `person` unit whose text is the stretch without the whitespace at its ends, or no unit when the stretch holds only whitespace, which is an **empty person**, a null element of the task's people (see [JourneyTaskStatement](../ast/journey.md#journeytaskstatement)).
patterns.name: punctuation.separator.comma.mermaid

patterns.comment: Read the third colon and the rest of the data as ignored text, with no inherited score or people string scope. journey.md#tasks: From the third colon, the rest of the data is an `ignored-data` unit, the colon included and the whitespace at its end left out, which mermaid.js does not read: `A: 3: a,b: c, d` has the people `a` and `b`, and `: c, d` is not read; `A: 5: Me:` has the ignored text `:`, `A: 5: Me: x: y` the ignored text `: x: y`, and `A: 5: Me: x` followed by two spaces the ignored text `: x`.
Read an entity whole and preserve the enclosing value scope and internal directive scopes. common.md#entities: Entities do not overlap.

journey-acc-descr-block.comment: Read a case-insensitive accessibility block and text delimiters, retaining directives in its whitespace. journey.md#the-statement-context: `accDescr`, zero or more whitespace characters, line feeds included, `{`, and zero or more whitespace characters, line feeds included: an `accDescr` unit and a `{` unit; enters the description block context.

journey-accessibility-line.comment: Read accessibility line values after their leading padding, retaining inline percent pairs. journey.md#accessibility-values: In the title context and in the description context, the one rule is: one or more characters other than a line feed: an `acc-title-text` unit in the title context, an `acc-description-text` unit in the description context; leaves the context.

journey-hash-comment.comment: Read a native hash comment, ending before a separator-led common comment. journey.md#the-statement-context: `#`: a diagram comment, from the `#` to the end of the line (see [Comments](#comments)).

comment: Keep diagram-specific text ends and whitespace gaps in this file; shared forms remain common includes and variables. journey.md#units-and-contexts: Whitespace in this document is the set of [Notation](../common.md#notation): U+00A0, U+2028, U+3000, U+FEFF, a vertical tab, and a form feed are whitespace wherever a rule reads whitespace, and so is a line feed where a rule says so.
